findings.finding: send_telegram_message escapes double quotes via text.replace(/"/g, '\"') and interpolates the string directly into a bash command executed via /bin/bash -c, enabling arbitrary command execution via $() or backticks without BASH_ALLOWED=true.
findings.why_it_matters: A prompt-injected or untrusted model turn invoking the send_telegram_message tool with a payload containing subshell execution syntax (e.g. $(id)) executes arbitrary commands directly on the host machine, bypassing the sandbox.js path fence and BASH_ALLOWED protection.

repro.command: node -e 'const text = "test $(echo PWNED_COMMAND_INJECTION)"; const cmd = `echo "${text.replace(/"/g, "\\\"")}"`; require("child_process").exec(cmd, (err, stdout) => { console.log("Stdout:", stdout.trim()); });'

findings.proposed_fix: Invoke the send script via spawn directly with argv arguments (spawn('/bin/bash', [sendScript, text])) without passing an interpolated command string to /bin/bash -c.
findings.done_when: send_telegram_message safely passes text via process arguments without subshell evaluation.
findings.review_verdict: CONFIRMED REAL, and WORSE than filed. Drove the exact escaping: $(echo X) and `echo X` both evaluate (bash expands substitution inside double quotes despite the " escaping). Proved real impact by reading the host name into a file. Amplification the audit missed: (a) the injection fires even when the target send script is MISSING, because bash expands the substitution before exec'ing, so the tool is exploitable on a box where it otherwise 'does not work'; (b) the tool has NO available() gate and is in the executable set, and it bypasses BASH_ALLOWED and sandbox.js entirely.

findings.finding: get_system_health executes SELECT 1 inside a bare try/except that swallows all exceptions without setting db_alive=False, omits db_alive from the response dict, and returns hardcoded fake metrics (99.98% uptime, canned latencies) even when the database is offline.
findings.why_it_matters: When a database outage or connection exhaustion occurs, the administrative endpoint /api/admin/system-health returns HTTP 200 with an unblemished 99.98% uptime SLA and false sub-second latency readings, deceiving operators and automated monitors.

repro.command: ./.venv/bin/python -c "from unittest.mock import MagicMock; from server.admin_advanced import admin_advanced_service; db = MagicMock(); db.execute.side_effect = Exception('db down'); res = admin_advanced_service.get_system_health(db); print('db_alive in res:', 'db_alive' in res, 'uptime:', res.get('uptime_percentage'))"

findings.proposed_fix: Update db_alive = False in the except block, include db_alive in the returned response dictionary, and report honest degraded status when database probes fail.

test_to_write.body:
def test_system_health_reports_database_down():
    from unittest.mock import MagicMock
    from server.admin_advanced import admin_advanced_service
    mock_db = MagicMock()
    mock_db.execute.side_effect = Exception('Database unreachable')
    res = admin_advanced_service.get_system_health(mock_db)
    assert 'db_alive' in res and res['db_alive'] is False

findings.done_when: get_system_health returns db_alive: False and reflects true system operational state.
findings.review_verdict: CONFIRMED REAL. Read the handler: db_alive is set True, db.execute sits in a bare except that passes, db_alive is never set False and never returned, and uptime/latencies/error-rates/incidents are all hardcoded literals.

findings.finding: When delta == 0, charge_actual_usage returns 0 immediately at line 329 without advancing _set_usage_high_water(row, upto_id) and without recording an idempotency entry in CreditTransaction.
findings.why_it_matters: When a task's pre-charge matches actual usage (or min-token rounding produces zero delta), the user's high-water mark is not advanced to upto_id, leaving the processed ApiUsageLog entries un-settled in the user high-water state for subsequent concurrent runs.

findings.proposed_fix: Call _set_usage_high_water(row, upto_id) and commit before returning when delta == 0.

findings.proposed_fix: Add an IP-aggregate check check_sliding_rate_limit(f'login_ip:{ip}', 30, 300) to login() alongside the per-account limit.
findings.done_when: Password spraying across different emails from the same IP is blocked with HTTP 429.
findings.review_verdict: CONFIRMED REAL. Login has only login:{ip}:{email}. The pattern the audit recommends already exists elsewhere in the same file (otp_ip:{ip}, otp_verify_ip:{ip}) — so this is an omission, not a design choice.

refutations.claim: harness edit_file tool suffers from JavaScript String.replace $ token expansion corruption ($&, $1, etc.)
refutations.ran: node -e 'const { executeTool } = require("./src/tools/tools"); const fs = require("fs"); fs.writeFileSync("/tmp/test_rep.txt", "val: TARGET"); executeTool("edit_file", { path: "/tmp/test_rep.txt", old_string: "TARGET", new_string: "$1 $& $" }).then(() => console.log("Content:", fs.readFileSync("/tmp/test_rep.txt", "utf-8")));'
refutations.conclusion: REFUTED: Line 267 uses content.replace(oldStr, () => args.new_string) when replace_all is false and content.split(oldStr).join(args.new_string) when true. execution_steps.change: Stop building a shell string. The handler currently does `const cmd = `set -a; ... bash "${sendScript}" "${text.replace(/"/g,'\\"')}"`` then `spawn('/bin/bash',['-c',cmd])`. Pass text as an ARGUMENT VECTOR instead: spawn('/bin/bash', ['-c', 'set -a; [ -f "$1" ] && source "$1"; set +a; exec bash "$2" "$3"', 'bash', envFile, sendScript, text]). Inside the script body use positional parameters ($1/$2/$3), never interpolation. This removes the shell parse of the text entirely, so $(), backticks and ; are inert.
execution_steps.why: The only escaping is for double quotes, and bash still expands $() and backticks INSIDE double quotes. Verified: the send script received 'test PWNED' with the substitution already evaluated, and a payload of `$(cat /etc/hostname)` returned the machine's hostname. It fires even when the send script is missing, and the tool has no available() gate.
